title: Annual trend tests keep DOISST correction ratios bounded but leave four HadISST1 window ratios unbounded
abstract: We tested whether small SST trends prevent bounded estimates of published SST pattern feedbacks. We used annual aggregate series and five model Green's functions for fixed ice-free ocean at 60 S to 60 N. Approximate 95% Fieller sets use covariance from 10,000 paired residual block draws. Raw DOISST and two published corrections have bounded sets in all 21 sliding windows of 21 years ending in 2002-2022, with two-, three- and five-year blocks. HadISST1 has unbounded sets in four windows with three-year blocks, and in two windows with all three block lengths. Thus, this test supports the DOISST result but limits interpretation of extreme HadISST1 ratios. The undivided radiative pattern trend also separates a direct pattern effect from denominator sensitivity. For the OI v2 2018 step in 2001-2022, its five-model mean change is -0.0269 W m-2 per decade, with a paired interval of -0.0428 to -0.0115; every model interval excludes zero. This effect survives removal of division by SST warming. The DOISST ratio effect during slow warming is mainly a denominator effect that a smaller direct pattern effect opposes. No new SST observations are used. Confidence coverage is approximate and omits correction and model uncertainty.
